nodes.label: Ask the graph before you search
nodes.norm_label: ask the graph before you search
nodes.rationale: graphify query/path/explain before a grep or source read, then read only the lines it points to.

nodes.label: The manifest is generated
nodes.rationale: After a tool changed in the core, npm run build && npm run manifest; manifest.test.ts fails on a stale one; a changed manifest needs --accept-capabilities on the next reload.

nodes.label: Care with a real backend
nodes.rationale: The tools write into a mod manager's instance: work on a test instance, change other people's mods only through patches, ask before deploying into a played profile.

nodes.label: A tool fails by throwing (core's message as plain text)
nodes.norm_label: a tool fails by throwing (core's message as plain text)
nodes.rationale: OpenClaw writes the thrown message into its own JSON, so JSON in the message would be escaped twice (every path backslash four); nothing goes into details that OpenClaw would grade, since a non-success status there fails the call.

nodes.label: Update the graph after every change
nodes.norm_label: update the graph after every change
nodes.rationale: graphify update . for code in its own commit; changed documents or images need /graphify --update; only graph.json and .graphify_labels.json are in git.

nodes.label: Install OpenClaw step (openclaw@2026.10.7, global)
nodes.rationale: The host: npm install links it for the SDK's types (scripts/link-openclaw.mjs).

nodes.norm_label: test job (ubuntu-24.04 + windows-latest matrix: test:types, test, build)

nodes.label: Build check only logs its request
nodes.norm_label: build check only logs its request
nodes.rationale: The build check's extra pass never happens in a run that called a plugin tool or wrote a file, because OpenClaw revises only runs it could replay.

nodes.label: A changed config schema needs a gateway restart, not a reload
nodes.norm_label: a changed config schema needs a gateway restart, not a reload
nodes.rationale: The running gateway checks the config against the schema it loaded, refuses the new fields as invalid, and so refuses the reload that would bring the new schema.

nodes.label: OpenClaw is the host, not a dependency
nodes.norm_label: openclaw is the host, not a dependency
nodes.rationale: The gateway supplies openclaw/plugin-sdk at runtime, so OpenClaw is never added to dependencies; .npmrc keeps npm from installing it as a peer.

nodes.label: Skills come from the core
nodes.rationale: skills/ is rebuilt from node_modules/skyrim-modding-tools-core and never edited; the manifest names skills/Domain/skills and OpenClaw links them into plugin-skills when the gateway starts.

nodes.label: ADR-0009 (core): hooks in the plugin, nearest MCP equivalent
nodes.norm_label: adr-0009 (core): hooks in the plugin, nearest mcp equivalent
nodes.rationale: What only OpenClaw can do (a hook) stays in the plugin; the MCP server gets the nearest equivalent where one exists.

nodes.label: ClawHub package (staged, core bundled)
nodes.rationale: ClawHub installs with npm install --ignore-scripts, which would leave a github: core without dist/ or helper, so the package is staged with the core bundled at its exact version, never this checkout.

nodes.norm_label: upgrading to a new core release

nodes.label: Core-first principle
nodes.rationale: A change to a tool, an answer, a guide or a skill is made in the core, never only here, so the plugin and the MCP server stay in step; this repo holds only OpenClaw's glue.

nodes.label: SkyrimHelper.exe (Windows helper launcher)
nodes.rationale: The application host with the CET opt-out Mod Organizer's virtual file system needs.
